dropped.name: ox
dropped.reason: A single ox seen side-on can't show its yoke. The bar and bow read as a box sitting on the cow's back. A trace line running back looked like a slash through the body. The yoke only reads with a pair of oxen, which breaks the one-figure rule.

dropped.name: sloth
dropped.reason: Seen front-on, hanging from a branch, it reads as the orangutan (same pose) or as a pot on a bar. In profile, the arms up to the branch read as a table with a face. The eye masks need more room than a 24 px face has: drawn small they looked like a skull or a propeller.

dropped.name: mole
dropped.reason: The spade paws and snout read as a crab or crown from the front, and as a fin or hand in profile. The molehill alone doesn't say mole, and front-on eye dots made the head look like a skull.

dropped.name: sheep-ram
dropped.reason: The curled horn sits on top of the head. Drawn as a piece on top, the engine's clearance around it cut the muzzle off into a loose fragment at every weight. Drawn without that clearance, the curl crossed the head outline and left slivers that closed at weight 2.1.

I drew 88 of the 92 approved icons in the new file /Users/andrevalleortega/Desktop/flouvia-icons/src/icons/animales.mjs. It is the only file I touched (git status shows only it as new), and I didn't commit, push, create any i18n files or read anything in ~/Desktop/flouvia. The file imports only ../../engine/geometry.mjs and transform from ../../engine/variants.mjs. It ends with the export using the label 'Animales', which matches src/taxonomy.json.

Checks, all on the final file:
- `node scripts/build.mjs --check animales`: 88 valid icons. The only remaining errors are the i18n "missing" ones, which belong to the language agent.
- `node scripts/qa.mjs animales` (full run, including the near-duplicate check against the whole set): 88 icons checked, 0 warnings. After it started I only moved the 16 px block and corrected one comment, with no geometry changes.
- `node scripts/weights-sheet.mjs animales`: every icon keeps its structure from 0.9 to 2.1.
- The sheet's live-area check is clean.
- Sheets regenerated and reviewed: previews/animales-1..3.png and previews/animales-variantes-1..3.png. I also reviewed a true-pixel 16 px rasterization.

How the drawings are built:
- Every whole animal stands in profile, facing right, on one ground line (20.25, the height mascotas' cat-seated and dog-seated sit on). Each body is one closed outline, as in mascotas' dog-side.
- Lean animals stand on stroke legs, 3 apart in pairs. Heavy ones (bears, elephant, mammoth, hippo, rhino, gorilla, kangaroo) have their legs drawn into the outline.
- Families share one body: the big cats, the bears, the bovines, the horses (zebra, donkey and unicorn build on the horse), the deer, the goats and the camels.
- The faces are front-on heads on the bear-market/emociones proportions: r 0.5 dot eyes, with the telling feature (mane, stripes, patches, horns, fringe) drawn large.
- Badges are the engine's: alert on bear and cow, plus on cow. A few pieces sit on top as custom badges so the engine clears what's underneath (the mammoth's tusk, the red panda's body over its tail).
- Every icon has tags (at least four, Spanish and English) and fill (solid, cut, wire or lines). Parts are set on all of them.
- Motion is set where there's a natural gesture: tails wag, runners slide, leapers bounce, hanging animals swing, the sleeping bear breathes, badges wiggle.
- No mirror: the animals keep their side, as in mascotas.
- variants are off only for deer-crossing, which is already enclosed.
- small drawings were added for hoof-print and lion-face. Everything else reads acceptably at true 16 px after snapping.

Compromises made to keep structure stable across weights:
- Every corner on a closed outline is at least 0.6 radius.
- Tail tufts end at the dot's centre.
- The panda's eye patches are solid dots.
- lion-face has no inner ears, and the unicorn horns are slim spikes.
- bull and bison lost their tails, and the deer keeps one tine.
- deer-crossing shows an antlerless doe drawn at the sign's own scale.
- The skunk's stripe was dropped.

Weaker icons a reviewer may want to redraw: groundhog (reads somewhat like a teddy bear), beaver, platypus, raccoon, deer-crossing, saddle and bear-standing.
